conclusions: Cocos IDs are not arbitrary equality-only tokens: HFP equal-heal selection uses Object.keys numeric index order, choosing the first maximum through a strict greater-than comparison. Arbitrary identity renaming can change the consumed buff and combat result.

Order-preserving positive integer renaming below the array-index limit may preserve some gameplay decisions, but HFP sparse-array length still changes and is part of full mutable state. This is not a passed renaming proof.
The original-source regression in tools/tests/cocos-identity.test.mjs demonstrates both the combat tie change from reversing ID order and the full-state array-length change from monotone compaction.

Other enumerated identity-keyed containers, key-range boundaries, local truthiness/sentinels, escaped fields, renderer/debug string conversion and arbitrary helper callees remain obligations before any semantic ID type/projection can be adopted.
Logical entity IDs/index_in_engine and gameplay counters are a separate domain; no numerical normalization is applied.

classManagerProof.implication: Generated class constructors share one monotonically incremented numeric instance counter with render objects. Logical entity IDs/index_in_engine are a separate domain and must not be normalized.

limitations: Only sourceRecords-extracted expressions are parsed; complete module literal counts retain potential uncovered top-level uses.
Local bindings/conditional value flow are followed; model-field escapes and arbitrary callees require further interprocedural proof.
Numeric array keys affect length, holes and key enumeration. Identity-key candidates alone do not establish renaming invariance.
Raw numeric __instanceId values remain part of full mutable-state/f64 traces; no normalization is authorized or applied.
